## Setup

```{r eval = FALSE}
devtools::install()
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tripaccess)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Single Table Wrangling and Data Visualization Example

This example uses the `house` dataset to explore household vehicle access. The
main question is whether households with more drivers tend to have more
vehicles.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = "70%"}
#> Filtered to households with at least one driver
house_with_drivers <- house |>
  filter(number_drivers > 0)

#> Create readable labels for Census division and young child status
house_with_drivers <- house_with_drivers |>
  mutate(
    region_label = case_when(
      region == "01" ~ "New England",
      region == "02" ~ "Middle Atlantic",
      region == "03" ~ "East North Central",
      region == "04" ~ "West North Central",
      region == "05" ~ "South Atlantic",
      region == "06" ~ "East South Central",
      region == "07" ~ "West South Central",
      region == "08" ~ "Mountain",
      region == "09" ~ "Pacific"
    ),
    young_child_status = case_when(
      count_young_child > 0 ~ "Young child in household",
      TRUE ~ "No young child in household"
    )
  )

#> Sort facet_wrap labels
house_with_drivers$region_sort_val <- factor(house_with_drivers$region_label, levels = c("New England", "Middle Atlantic", "East North Central", "West North Central", "South Atlantic", "East South Central", "West South Central", "Mountain", "Pacific"))

#> Plot household vehicles by Census division
ggplot(data = house_with_drivers,
       aes(x = number_vehicles)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~region_sort_val) +
  labs(title = "Household Vehicle Counts by Census Division",
       x = "Number of Household Vehicles",
       y = "Count of Households") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 4),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 5),
        title = element_text(size = 5))

#> Summary statistics of vehicles by number of drivers
house_with_drivers |>
  group_by(number_drivers) |>
  summarize(
    households = n(),
    mean_vehicles = mean(number_vehicles),
    median_vehicles = median(number_vehicles),
    sd_vehicles = sd(number_vehicles)
  )

#> Filtered to households with at least one vehicle
house_with_vehicles <- house_with_drivers |>
  filter(number_vehicles > 0)

#> Plot household vehicles by number of drivers
ggplot(data = house_with_vehicles,
       aes(x = number_drivers,
           y = number_vehicles)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.08, width = 0.15, height = 0.15) +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, formula = y ~ x, color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Household Vehicles by Number of Drivers",
       x = "Number of Drivers in Household",
       y = "Number of Household Vehicles") +
  theme_bw()

#> Fit a simple linear regression model
vehicles_drivers_model <- lm(number_vehicles ~ number_drivers,
                             data = house_with_vehicles)
summary(vehicles_drivers_model)

#> Correlation between number of drivers and number of vehicles
cor(house_with_vehicles$number_drivers, house_with_vehicles$number_vehicles)

#> The slope estimates the average change in household vehicles for one
#> additional driver in the household.
coef(vehicles_drivers_model)["number_drivers"]

#> Compare vehicle access across Census divisions
house_with_vehicles |>
  group_by(region_label) |>
  summarize(
    households = n(),
    mean_vehicles = mean(number_vehicles),
    median_vehicles = median(number_vehicles)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_vehicles))

#> Plot Household Vehicle Counts by Young Child Status
ggplot(data = house_with_vehicles,
       aes(x = number_vehicles,
           y = young_child_status,
           fill = young_child_status)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~region_sort_val) +
  labs(title = "Household Vehicle Counts \nBy Young Child Status",
       fill = "Young Child Status",
       x = "Number of Household Vehicles",
       y = "Young Child Status") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 2),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 4),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 4),
        title = element_text(size = 4),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 4),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 4)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("indianred1", "palegreen3"))
```
